messages:
From: Daniel Brooks <daniel.brooks@sabletx.com>

Subject: Sable RFI — compact operator runbook and VPC questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this on. We're compiling answers for our internal security board and procurement team and trying to keep the packet concise. Attached is our RFI (Sable-RFI-v3.pdf) — the items we care most about for a Private deployment are: operator onboarding and permissions, offline/air-gapped update process, egress controls and evidence of no uncontrolled telemetry, and a compact operator runbook (we need something operator-facing, 2–4 pages, that an on-call sysadmin can follow).

The RFI has 12 short questions; can you provide an annotated response and the compact runbook diagram by end of day TOMORROW? If possible, include a network segmentation diagram showing required subnets and peering. If any items need procurement or SOC2 evidence, flag them.

Appreciate the help — happy to set a 30-min tech call if that helps.

Thanks,
Daniel Brooks
Head of Platform Security
Sable Therapeutics

Subject: Re: Sable RFI — compact operator runbook and VPC questions

Hi Daniel — thanks for the RFI and the clear priorities. We prepared an annotated response to the 12 items and a compact operator runbook aimed at on-call/sysadmin operators (attached). Highlights here for quick triage: 

- Operator runbook (attached: redwood-compact-runbook-v1.2.pdf): a 3-page step-through covering start/stop of serving nodes, emergency model rollback, operator escalation flow, and rolling patch acceptance for air-gapped sites. It includes exact kubectl/systemctl snippets where applicable and a minimal checklist for acceptance testing.

- Offline/air-gapped updates: we support signed update bundles. Our recommended process: (1) Redwood produces a signed bundle and SBOM, (2) customer pulls bundle into airlock media and verifies signature against public-key thumbprint, (3) operator runs the built-in package installer which verifies integrity and applies update. We included a patch signature verification example in the runbook.

- Egress & telemetry: by default telemetry is disabled in Private. When enabled (customer opt-in) we collect only operational metrics (cpu/mem/io, per-node request counts) and post to customer-configured telemetry endpoints inside the VPC; no token-level text or prompts are exfiltrated. The network diagram (attached: network-segmentation-diagram.png) shows the control-plane tunnel (optional), model-serving subnets, operator bastion, and a blocked egress enforcement point for customers requiring 0 outbound.

- Operator permissions & service accounts: we recommend a least-privilege operator service account bound to a small set of actions: start/stop service, read logs, rotate keys (via KMS gateway) and perform canary rollback. The runbook includes a permission matrix (Operator, SRE, Security Reviewer) and example IAM/YAML snippets for both AWS and on-prem RBAC.

- KMS/HSM integration: we support KMS via customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM attestations for on-prem. Key wraps happen locally; Redwood's control plane (if used) never retains plaintext keys. We included sample API calls and a note about integrating with on-prem HSMs (PKCS#11).

- Evidence & procurement flags: SOC2 Type II reports and our private-deploy acceptance criteria checklist are available upon execution of an NDA / DPA. For procurement, Marissa is copied to coordinate SOW and any redlines.

Attachments: redwood-compact-runbook-v1.2.pdf, network-segmentation-diagram.png, rfi-response-checklist.xlsx

Next steps we propose: 1) I can send the annotated RFI answers (inline) within the hour; 2) schedule a 30-min technical walk-through (I suggest Wed morning PDT); 3) Marissa can start procurement paperwork if the checklist looks good.

Let me know whether to proceed with an inline annotated RFI now or hand off to a walkthrough.

Best,
Irene Choi

Irene — this is excellent, thanks. A couple of clarifying items from our security reviewer: 

1) For the air-gapped patch flow, can you confirm the cryptographic signature algorithm and whether we can use our HSM-stored key for verification on the appliance? We need explicit example commands that our operators can run during verification.

2) In the permission matrix, what exact actions are required for a rollback (i.e., which API calls or system actions need to be permitted)? Our auditors want a minimal ACL to sign off.

3) The network diagram looks good; can you add an explicit callout for allowed DNS resolution and whether the service expects outbound connections for CRL/OCSP checks? We may need to allow selective DNS resolution only during installation.

If you could add those three items to the runbook and reply with the updated snippets, that should cover our board. Also — we will likely require a signed mutual NDA before we exchange SOC2 artifacts; Marissa, please coordinate with your legal team.

Thanks — DM

Subject: Re: Sable RFI — compact operator runbook and VPC questions

Daniel / Irene — quick follow-up from engineering. Answers inline to Daniel's three clarifying points:

1) Signature algorithm / HSM: we use RSA-4096 with SHA-256 signatures for bundles by default; we can also provide ECDSA-P-256 signatures on request. Your on-prem verifier can validate signatures using OpenSSL/PKCS11 against an HSM-resident keypair. Example verification command (bundle.tar.sig attached in runbook):

   openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public_key.pem -signature bundle.tar.sig bundle.tar

   If you're validating against an HSM-protected key, you can use pkcs11-tool / pkcs11-provider with the same openssl invocation via engine_pkcs11. We included a step-by-step HSM verification snippet in redwood-compact-runbook-v1.2.pdf (section 2.3).

2) Rollback ACLs: minimal actions required for rollback are: DescribeModelVersion (read), StopServingInstance, ReplaceModelArtifact, StartServingInstance, and ReadLogs. Example roles: operator.rollback (Start/Stop/Replace), operator.view (ReadLogs, DescribeModelVersion). The runbook includes exact API endpoints and Kubernetes job names for both managed and on-prem installers.

3) DNS / CRL behavior: the installer by default performs OCSP/CRL checks during installation if outbound connectivity is available. For strict air-gapped installs, the installer accepts a local CRL bundle and an explicit --offline flag to bypass online checks (we then require a signed attestation and timestamp). We added a callout in the network diagram and runbook showing the small set of resolver endpoints used for optional checks; installers will not attempt arbitrary outbound connections beyond those.

We'll produce a 2nd iteration of the runbook with the HSM command examples and the minimal ACLs. Suggested next step: schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough (we can do Wed 08:00–11:00 PDT). Marissa — can you confirm NDA path and whether Sable will be using a vendor-specific procurement template?
